original_test_intent: Configure an AMI OEM virtual CD instance, or inspect that action, with the preserved source ambiguously presenting a state-changing action as a Get/GET request.
original_method: After resolving the method conflict and obtaining the AMI schema, configure exactly one approved CD instance with a verified image/source and persistence/boot scope, validate resulting state, then run the documented unconfigure/eject restoration.
manual_activity: Resolve GET versus POST, supply the AMI payload schema, select the exact CD instance and approved image/source, define persistence and host boot/device impact, and approve cleanup/recovery.
required_inputs: Exact payload field types and allowed values
Sanitized access method for the image
Baseline CD/VirtualMedia and host boot/device state
Trusted TLS and privileged credential handle
safety_requirements: Never run the source GET as an action
No automatic retry after ambiguous status
agent_execution_scope: Bind BMC, Manager, CD device, image and firmware identity
Read OEM action metadata and baseline state
Validate configured CD and host-visible device state
Compare approved fields and unrelated state to baseline
engineer_actions: Approve OEM payload, target, image, persistence and boot impact

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A POST likely matches action semantics, but it materially changes the Master GET and cannot be executed without the AMI schema, exact CD/image target and restore contract.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With an approved AMI contract, submit one exact POST for the selected CD instance, validate resulting BMC and host state, then unconfigure/eject and prove restoration; inspect read-only after any ambiguous timeout.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Manager-scoped OEM action and 15/10 timing remain; no payload, device mapping, image source, persistence or cleanup is inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat ConfigureCDInstance as a bounded configuration transaction with immutable image identity and a tested inverse operation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the GET/POST conflict explicit and adds OEM schema, device/image binding, persistence/boot analysis, one-shot semantics and field-level restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers AMI CD-instance configuration only; it does not prove general InsertMedia, EjectMedia or boot-install behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An OEM setting may persist beyond session or BMC reboot, and ejecting media may not clear the configured source; cleanup must use the vendor-defined inverse, not assumptions.

project_override_considerations: If ConfigureCDInstance only stages configuration while a separate enable action activates it, evidence must distinguish staged and active states. Generic Redfish VirtualMedia fields cannot replace the AMI OEM schema.
expected_evidence: AMI schema revision, canonical action URI and exact redacted payload
Approved image identity/hash and sanitized source
Approval, persistence/boot decision and maintenance context
Unconfigure/eject result and restored field-by-field baseline

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item and Procedure say Get and send GET, but the URI is an AMI OEM action and DeepSeek/GPT V2 interpret it as POST. The execution method and resulting state differ materially, so this is a source conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The OEM schema, target/image choices, approvals and cleanup are identifiable prerequisites; the action is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Converts a misleading OEM GET into a controlled, reversible-by-contract CD configuration transaction with image integrity and host-impact evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: ConfigureCDInstance is not interchangeable with InsertMedia: it may stage a persistent AMI configuration, select a device instance, or bind a remote image independently of current insertion state. Therefore the exact OEM fields and inverse operation are essential. A generic POST plus HTTP status cannot prove the intended CD device was configured or that boot behavior remained unchanged. The review requires immutable image identity, readback of the configured state, host device observation and cleanup that restores each approved baseline field. Ambiguous completion is resolved through read-only state inspection, never a blind second POST.
